newsitem.title: USA: Officers removed in illegal Carvel stock deal.
newsitem.headline: Officers removed in illegal Carvel stock deal.

text.p: Two officers of the Thomas and Agnes Carvel Foundation, created in 1976 by the ice cream magnate and his wife, will step down to settle charges they engineered an illegal stock deal, the New York State Attorney General said Tuesday.

Mildred Arcadipane, vice president and secretary of the foundation and former corporate secretary of the Carvel Corp., and Robert Davis, president and counsel to the foundation, resigned to resolve allegations they sold Carvel Corp. stock to a favoured group of Carvel employees.

The state sued the defendants in 1993 after an investigation by the Attorney General's office allegedly revealed that Arcadipane and Davis engineered the sale of 115,200 shares of Carvel Corp. stock from the foundation to a group comprised of Carvel Corp. employees including Arcadipane.

Less than a year later, the investment group was able to sell the shares it had acquired to Cream Acquisition, Inc., the purchaser of the corporation, for $90 per share, which is more than twice what the foundation received for the same stock.

Arcadipane also agreed to repay the foundation $57,000, representing personal profits as a result of the stock transfers. She previously repaid $25,000 to the foundation that the lawsuit charged went to finance private school tuition for her nephew.
The Carvel Foundation, based in Yonkers, N.Y., has assets over $15 million and provides grants for charitable, educational, religious, scientific, literary and cultural groups.
